question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Break a leg
solution:
The correct answer is: **"Good luck."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**Break a leg**" is an idiom commonly used in theatre to wish someone good luck before a performance.
 
• The phrase originated from the superstition that wishing someone good luck before a performance would actually bring bad luck, so saying the opposite (i.e. "break a leg") would reverse the luck.
 
• This idiom is not meant to be taken literally and does not actually encourage harm to the person.
 
• The phrase can also be used outside of the theatre to wish someone good luck in a non-serious or humorous way.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "**Sudden attack**," is not related to the idiom "break a leg" and is not a commonly used meaning for this phrase.
 
• "**Accident**," is also not related to the idiom and is not a commonly used meaning for this phrase.
 
• "**Bravery**," is not related to the idiom and is not a commonly used meaning for this phrase.
